title: Video entertainment to mitigate safety risks during prolonged automated driving: Impacts on cognitive load, fatigue, and takeover performance
abstract: Studi simulasi menguji efek video entertainment terhadap kognitif load, kelelahan, dan kinerja takeover selama driving otomatis. Hasil menunjukkan video mengurangi kelelahan dan meningkatkan kinerja takeover, meskipun meningkatkan kognitif load.
objective: Menginvestigasi apakah video entertainment dapat mengurangi risiko kelelahan pasif selama driving otomatis dan meningkatkan kinerja takeover.
methods: Desain eksperimen 2x4 dalam-subjek dengan 32 peserta. Ukur kognitif load (pupil diameter, NASA-TLX), kelelahan (blink frequency, KSS), dan kinerja takeover (TOT, max acceleration, min TTC). Analisis menggunakan LMM.
context: Penelitian dilakukan di simulator driving otomatis tingkat 3, dengan peserta mengalami durasi otomatis 15-60 menit, dalam kondisi dengan atau tanpa video entertainment.
findings: Video mengurangi pertumbuhan kelelahan seiring waktu.
Video meningkatkan waktu minimum hingga tabrakan.
Kelelahan diukur melalui frekuensi blink dan skor KSS.
Kognitif load diukur melalui diameter pupil dan NASA-TLX.

concepts.name: passive task-related fatigue
concepts.description: Kelelahan akibat kondisi underloaded selama driving otomatis.

concepts.name: non-driving related tasks
concepts.description: Aktivitas yang tidak terkait dengan mengemudi, seperti menonton video.

concepts.name: takeover performance
concepts.description: Kinerja pengemudi saat mengambil kendali kembali dari sistem otomatis.

concepts.name: cognitive load
concepts.description: Beban kognitif yang diukur melalui diameter pupil dan skor NASA-TLX.

concepts.name: fatigue
concepts.description: Kelelahan yang diukur melalui frekuensi blink dan skor KSS.

concepts.name: linear mixed effects models
concepts.description: Metode statistik untuk menganalisis data berulang dengan efek acak peserta.

relationships.evidence: Video entertainment effectively suppressed the growth of fatigue with longer ADT.
Video entertainment reduced safety risks by shortening takeover time and increasing minimum time to collision.
Higher cognitive load usually leads to pupil dilation and higher NASA-TLX scores.
Prolonged disengagement may induce PTR fatigue, which may negatively impact takeover performance.
Video entertainment not only increased cognitive load, but also effectively suppressed the growth of fatigue.
Fatigue may negatively affect vigilance and impair takeover performance.
